title: NPPA Orders Strict Checks So Cancer Drug Price Cuts Reach Patients
excerpt: With revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs in force since November 9, the drug pricing authority has ordered strict enforcement checks; states including Andhra Pradesh have directed inspections of cancer hospitals and pharmacies.
body:
• The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has ordered strict checks to enforce the price cuts on 137 anti-cancer drugs, Mint reported, as the revised prices that took effect on November 9 are tested at pharmacy counters.
  • The cuts come from a 30% cap on trade margins: 76 companies reported revised MRPs for 1,225 formulations, with reductions in 1,031 formulations, 600 brands down by more than 50%, and the largest cut 96.45%, the government said.
  • The government estimates annual savings to consumers of Rs 3,502.31 crore — an official estimate based on reported prices, not an audit of patient bills.
  • What this means for you: before paying, check the drug's revised price on the Pharma Sahi Daam app or the NPPA website, and report any charge above the revised MRP to the NPPA.

India's drug pricing regulator has moved from announcing lower cancer medicine prices to policing them. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has ordered strict checks to enforce the price cuts on 137 anti-cancer drugs, Mint reported, days after the revised maximum retail prices took effect on November 9.

What was cut, and by how much

The intervention capped trade margins at 30% for 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, on the recommendation of an expert committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services. According to the Press Information Bureau release, 76 pharmaceutical companies reported revised MRPs for 1,225 formulations covering 121 drugs; prices fell in 1,031 formulations, 600 brands dropped by more than 50%, and the highest reported reduction was 96.45%. The list includes immunotherapy drugs used across more than 20 cancers, denosumab, pegfilgrastim and bevacizumab. The government put expected annual consumer savings at Rs 3,502.31 crore.

That savings figure needs reading carefully: it is the government's estimate from reported list prices. Whether patients actually pay less depends on what hospitals and pharmacies charge at the counter — which is what the enforcement push is meant to settle.

Enforcement reaches the states

In Andhra Pradesh, Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav directed drug inspectors to inspect all cancer hospitals within seven days, check that revised price lists have reached manufacturers' supply agents, and ensure hospitals display the lists at medicine counters and on their websites, Medical Buyer reported. Medicines must be sold at whichever is lower — the revised list price or the price printed on the pack — even where stock carries an older, higher printed MRP, the minister said, warning of strict action for overcharging.

How to check a price

Consumers can verify the applicable price of a cancer medicine through the Pharma Sahi Daam mobile application and the NPPA website, and report non-compliance or a charge above the revised MRP to the authority. The October 17 notification remains in force until further orders; manufacturers may take the annual price increase allowed under Paragraph 20(1) of the DPCO only while staying within the 30% trade margin cap.
image_caption: Capsules are piled in a close-up photograph. The NPPA has capped trade margins on 137 anti-cancer drugs and ordered strict checks that the revised prices are charged.
nri_angle: Families in India and relatives abroad who fund treatment can verify the legal price of a cancer medicine on the NPPA's Pharma Sahi Daam app before paying a pharmacy or hospital bill.
